- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–2% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following period; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.67 to 0.00 or vice versa), model exhibits lag; delay or smooth transition in forecast adjustment.
- Mean reversion is evident when model holds high prices for 3+ periods after a spike; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per period until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 forecast points.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast slope to match sentiment’s diminishing influence.
